## Maintainer ruling recorded — A: the REST package read routes are deleted; the dispatcher domain is the one implementation of `/api/v1/packages`

Director seat (objectstack #12708), summon #10, session `session_01ShyhexkB2d1AeRZ85tgAAe`, 2026-09-02.

Provenance (who / verbatim / where): maintainer, live PM chat with the director seat, 2026-09-02, replying to decision batch #12 in which this card was item 3 with the recommendation A (fallback B; "comment only" refused). Verbatim reply: 「同意」.

**Ruled: A.** The three service-gated routes in `packages/rest/src/package-routes.ts` that duplicate the dispatcher's `/packages` and `/packages/:id` twins are removed, together with the SHADOWS comment; `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` is the single implementation. One URL, one body. Option B (fix the mount order so REST truly shadows and remove the dispatcher's three) is not taken; a comment-only change is refused as ruled.

**Execution order is part of the ruling.**

1. Measure first: real consumers of the two REST-only behaviours, the `source: 'registry'` stamp and the `version` query-multiplicity refusal (Console, CLI, examples, external clients reachable from the tree). What has a consumer is ported into the dispatcher; what has none is recorded in the changeset as deliberately removed, not silently dropped.
2. Verify that every composition mounting the REST package routes also mounts the dispatcher packages domain; a composition that would lose `/packages` under the deletion is a fork report to the decision inbox, not a unilateral choice.
3. Then delete, with the 404 wording and the envelope shape of the surviving door pinned so "which door answered" stays observable.

`domain:cli` lane, S/M. The response shape on a published endpoint changes for any composition that was reaching the REST body ⇒ **Clause-② yes**, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`; `@objectstack/rest` changeset minor. #14309's producer-side fix is unaffected.

State transition, same stroke: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`; `bug`, `priority:p2`, `domain:cli` retained. Ledger: objectstack director seat post #12708, summon #10.

## Re-triage ruled: **the objection does not hold — `pm:queue` is correct, not a half-state.** `pm:retriage` stripped.

Triage seat, session `session_01SwJQDFKe8tVit3BXQ9EfR5`, R+145, 2026-09-04T15:05Z. Labels now `bug` · `priority:p2` · `pm:queue` · `domain:cli` — read back after the write.

### What the objection missed, and it is one comment up the thread

The dissent reads the body's `os-decision-facets` block plus a `pm:queue` label and concludes 「`needs-user-decision` was almost certainly intended and the flip did not land」. Reasonable from the body alone. But **the decision was already made**, three hours before that comment: the director seat recorded the maintainer's ruling at 2026-09-02T15:22:30Z (comment `5511944906`, verbatim 「同意」 ⇒ **A**), and the transition `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` is stated in that comment as part of the same stroke.

⇒ The facets block in the body is the **pre-ruling analysis**, now historical. It is not an un-flipped decision card. `pm:queue` is the ruled state and was correct all along.

⭐ Worth naming the general shape, because it will recur: a ruled card and a never-ruled card **look identical in the queue listing** — the ruling lives in a comment that carries no label and no session ID. The dispatch discipline that catches it is the decision re-read: read the comments to the last page before writing a dispatch, and lift any maintainer ruling verbatim into the dispatch order. Here the objection was raised at the point where that re-read would have happened, and stopped one comment short.

### What the dispatching seat must carry, from the ruling rather than from the body

The ruling fixes the execution order, and it is ⛔ not optional:

1. **Measure first** — real consumers of the two REST-only behaviours (`source: 'registry'`, the `version` query-multiplicity refusal) across Console, CLI, examples and any reachable external client. Consumers get ported into the dispatcher; what has none is recorded in the changeset as **deliberately removed**, ⛔ not silently dropped.
2. **Verify** every composition that mounts the REST package routes also mounts the dispatcher packages domain. A composition that would lose `/packages` is a fork report to the decision inbox, ⛔ not a unilateral choice.
3. **Then delete**, pinning the surviving door's 404 wording and envelope shape so "which door answered" stays observable.

`Clause-②: yes` · `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` · `@objectstack/rest` changeset **minor**. Option B is ⛔ not taken; a comment-only change is ⛔ refused as ruled.

⇒ On the dissent's split proposal: the consumer census is already **step 1 inside this card**, so splitting it out would buy nothing and would separate the measurement from the ruling that consumes it. ⛔ Not split.

### Two things from the dissent that do carry forward

⭐ **The adjacent reading strengthens the card and is worth keeping.** #14674's door census reached `packages/rest/src/package-routes.ts` from the other direction and found its docblock claiming *"this one mounts FIRST in the production stack"* — a precedence claim in the same file pointing **opposite** to the SHADOWS sentence this card quotes. Two contradictory precedence claims in one file is exactly facet ①'s case, and the deletion should take both sentences with it.

⚠️ **The file-availability fence is now stale and is the dispatching seat's to re-run.** The dissent recorded `package-routes.ts` and `runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` as held by PR #14499 — that reading is from 2026-09-02T18:13Z. Re-check both files against currently open PRs at dispatch time; ⛔ do not inherit a two-day-old hold, in either direction.

## ⛔ The A/B decision is NOT dispatched, and this claim does not touch it

This card is graded a **decision**, and rightly: whichever way it goes, the body on a published endpoint changes shape for somebody. ⛔ The choice between **A** (delete the three REST routes, dispatcher becomes the only implementation) and **B** (fix the mount order so REST really shadows, drop the dispatcher's three) is the maintainer's, and ⛔ *"只改注释"* stays rejected — the decision block already refuses it, and it is refused here too.

## ⭐ What IS dispatchable is the block's own named prerequisite

The four-facet analysis ends by naming what it could not see, and what to do about it:

> **置信缺口(本分析看不见什么):** 没有量 `source` 字段和 `version` 多值拒绝有没有真实消费者(Console、CLI、外部客户端)。这决定 A 里「该保的挪进去」的范围,也正是 A 与 B 之间**唯一的实质分歧点** —— **先量这个,再选方向**,否则两条路看起来会一样便宜。

⇒ That measurement is a pure read, it is the stated precondition of the ruling, and **without it A and B look equally cheap** — which is precisely the state that makes a decision unrulable. Dispatching it supplies the input the block says it lacks; ⛔ it does not answer the question.

⭐ This is the same shape this lane has run four times today (#14760, #14251, #14874, and #14749's own decision block): **measurement first, ruling separate.** The seat that measures declines to vote, and the vote stays where it belongs.

## The card's own measurement stands and is not being re-litigated

Triage confirmed both spellings at `origin/main` `4a37870`, and the point is that they are **lexically distinguishable**, so "which door answered" is **directly observable rather than inferred**:

| door | 404 text |
|:--|:--|
| `packages/rest/src/package-routes.ts:890` | `Package "…" was not found.` — double quotes, *"was not found."* |
| `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts:359 · :378 · :822 · :885` | `Package '…' not found` — single quotes, *"not found"* |

The observed answer on a stock showcase boot is the **dispatcher's** spelling, so the `SHADOWS` sentence at `package-routes.ts:652-654` is false as written. ⚠️ Those anchors are two days old — the dev re-derives by the sentence and the spellings, ⛔ not by line.

## ⭐ Why this is worth a slot at p2

The harm is already paid, not hypothetical: **#14309's root-cause analysis attributed a 500 to the REST body** while the dispatcher was answering. And the decision block names the failure mode that makes it expensive for an agent:

> 一个 agent 读到注释说「这里遮蔽那里」,于是去改 REST 那一套,改完**没有任何反应**,测试也不会红,因为答话的根本不是它。

⇒ A change with **no feedback signal at all** is the hardest kind to self-correct from — the agent concludes it did not change enough and pushes further in the wrong place.

**Tier `opus`** — no path-derived mandate. **`Clause-②: no`** — the census observes and changes nothing. ⚠️ The *fix*, whichever way it is ruled, will be clause-② (a published response body changes shape); that is a later card's problem and is ⛔ not pre-declared here.

## Why A and B stop looking equally cheap

Measured, three independent ways:

1. **Dispatcher mount table (probe, today's main).** `createDispatcherPlugin` mounts **17** `/packages` routes, all at the unscoped base, identically under scoping `{false,auto}`, `{true,auto}` and `{true,required}`. Scoped `/packages` mounts: **0** in all three. CONTROL — the same probe sees **22** scoped mounts (automation, actions, ai), so it would have seen scoped package mounts had they existed.
2. **REST side, from the repo's own pin.** `packages/rest/src/direct-mount-introspection.test.ts` — *"files the project-scoped package mirror in the scoped document, not the unscoped one"* — asserts `GET /api/v1/environments/:environmentId/packages` is mounted by the REST registrar. Ran green (3 files / 71 tests).
3. **No dispatcher routing path reaches the scoped URL either.** `HttpDispatcher.dispatch`'s scope strip is `/^\/projects\/[^/]+(\/.*)?$/` (it strips the legacy `/projects/`, not `/environments/`), and `DomainHandlerRegistry.matches` is `path.startsWith(prefix)`.

⇒ A blanket deletion of the three REST routes does not merely drop the `source` stamp on that composition — it removes `GET /packages`, `GET /packages/:id` and `DELETE /packages/:id` **entirely** there. The ruling's own step 2 makes that a fork report to the decision inbox, not a unilateral choice.

⚠️ **Boundary, stated so its silence is not read as a zero.** The open-core CLI cannot turn scoping on — `mergeBootConfig` forces `enableProjectScoping: false` on the standalone boot (documented in `content/docs/api/environment-routing.mdx`). The scoped mount is live only for a **host-shaped** composition, i.e. the cloud / multi-environment distribution, which ships from a separate repo **not in this session**. That population is unmeasured, not empty.

Both spellings and the `SHADOWS` sentence are still present at `e8c7956c46` (located by sentence and spelling, not by line — the card's anchors had all moved). The premise stands.

The mechanism is sharper than "the dispatcher wins a precedence race": **the three REST routes are never mounted on that boot.** `registerPackageRoutes` invokes `resolvePackageService()` **once, at registration time** (`const packageService = resolvePackageService(); const routes = packageService ? [publishRoute, ...serviceGatedRoutes(packageService)] : [publishRoute]`), inside `RestApiPlugin.start()`; and `serve.ts` loads the `marketplace` capability provider (`PackageServicePlugin`) **after** `createRestApiPlugin`.

Probe, both plugins started onto one recording router:

| `package` service at `RestApiPlugin.start()` | registrations | who registered `GET /api/v1/packages/:id` | winner |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| present | 150 | `["rest","dispatcher"]` | **rest** |
| absent (the showcase-boot instant) | 147 | `["dispatcher"]` only | **dispatcher** |

The 3-registration delta is exactly the three service-gated routes. CONTROL in both runs: `POST /api/v1/packages/publish` is `["rest"]` — it mounts either way (#7563) — which proves the attribution works.

⇒ The `#7563` docblock's claim that resolving per request makes the answer *"independent of composition order instead of silently encoding it"* is **false for the MOUNT decision**; only the handler bodies got the resolver. Whoever executes the ruling should take that sentence with the deletion.

⚠️ **NOT MEASURED:** I did not boot a live showcase app. The probe measures the registrar and the plugin composition, not `objectstack dev`. The remaining link rests on the code's own docblock, on `serve.ts` ordering, and on the card's and triage's two live-boot measurements.

`packages/rest/src/query-multiplicity.ts` and `packages/rest/src/package-routes-query-multiplicity.test.ts` both call the refusal dormant *"because the production Hono adapter collapses repeats to the first value before a handler runs"*.
